items.title: One function parses, validates, resolves duplicates, writes and reports
items.hit: Says importContacts mixes several jobs, with decisions and store writes interleaved in one loop, AND proposes a decomposition whose blocks it names by what they do: at least deciding what to import apart from writing it, or parse / validate / plan / write. A consequence is named: a rule cannot be tested or changed alone, or writes happen before the file is known to be good.
items.partial: Says the function is too long, too nested or does too much, and asks to split it, without naming the blocks.

items.title: The change re-implements CSV parsing that src/lib/csv.js already does
items.hit: Points at parseCsv in src/lib/csv.js as the existing parser and says to use it instead of the hand-written line and quote splitting.
items.partial: Criticises the hand-written parsing without naming the existing parser.

items.title: Email normalization and validation are re-implemented, and differ from the app's
items.hit: Says normalizeEmail / isEmail in src/contacts/email.js exist and are bypassed by the repeated `email.trim().toLowerCase()` or by the looser EMAIL_RE, so an address such as a@b is accepted here and refused by the single-contact form.
items.partial: Notes the repeated normalization expression or the second regular expression without the existing functions or the divergence.

items.title: Rows are written while the file is still being read
items.hit: Says contacts are inserted or renamed inside the parsing loop, so a file that turns out unparsable, or a strict-mode throw, leaves earlier rows written, against 'nothing is written if the file cannot be parsed'; or says an unclosed quote is never detected at all.

items.title: The same email twice in a file is counted as a create and an update
items.hit: Says a repeated email in one file is created by its first row and then renamed by the next, so it is counted twice, against 'counts once'.

items.title: The mode option and the insert retry serve nothing
items.hit: Says at least one of: options.mode with its strict and legacy branches has no caller and no requirement; the retry loop around store.insert assumes a failure that an in-memory store does not have, and then drops the row silently.
items.partial: Mentions one of them as odd without calling it removable.

items.title: Addresses of one domain are skipped silently
items.hit: Points at the `@example.invalid` skip marked temporary: no requirement asks for it, and its rows are neither imported nor reported.

items.hit: Names at least one requirement no test covers (a repeated email, an unparsable file, the reported line and reason, case-insensitive match) or says the tests pin behavior nobody asked for (strict, legacy, the skipped domain, the rows field).
